title: Kernel continuity and state reconciliation manual
author: Priya Ranganathan
content:
Purpose:
This manual describes the operational controls, instrumentation, and step-by-step runbooks for maintaining kernel continuity across live kernel handoffs, preemptive evictions, and cross-node failover. It focuses on deterministic state reconciliation of KV caches, token-level prefix state, and quantization metadata to avoid model drift, duplicate generation, or silent correctness regressions during runtime transitions.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: runtime oncall, runtime engineers, release engineers, and SREs responsible for kernel rollouts and incident recovery.
- Scope: live kernel swaps, preemption and eviction events, cross-NUMA/node handoffs, and scripted rollback scenarios. Does NOT cover model-level content validation or developer sandbox experiments (see related pages).

Goals and SLO constraints:
- Preserve deterministic generation for pinned sessions where possible: session_replay_agreement >= 99.9% within 2s of handoff under nominal load.
- Maintain 99th percentile latency SLOs within configured degradation targets (see table "Operational thresholds").
- Avoid silent semantic regressions: any handoff that changes generation tokens for >0.1% of validation prompt set must trigger an audit and canary rollback.

Definitions (quick):
- Kernel instance: runtime binary + kernel plugins that schedule and execute attention kernels.
- KV state: Key/value caches (kv_cache) containing past key/value tensors and session metadata used to accelerate autoregressive generation.
- Continuity window: time range where in-flight requests must be consistent across old and new kernel variants.
- Deterministic reconcile: process that ensures two kernel instances produce identical logits for an identical prefix.

Architecture overview (text diagram):
- Ingress -> Request classification (priority, session pin) -> Kernel router -> Kernel pool (GPU shards)
  - Each kernel has local KV cache + shared persistent session index (Session Index backed by Redis/etcd).
  - Handoff path: kernel A (source) -> cooperative drain -> state snapshot -> kernel B (target) -> verify -> commit -> update router.

Key invariants to enforce:
1) Snapshot completeness: all active KV ranges referenced by sessions must be included in the snapshot (no partial references).
2) Sequence monotonicity: session token counters must not decrease across handoffs.
3) Quantization metadata fidelity: quantization scale/zero-point and per-layer layout metadata must accompany tensors.
4) Observability trace IDs must be preserved across Gs (gateway) to kernel transitions.

Operational thresholds (table):
- SLO / Threshold / Action
- session_replay_agreement >= 99.9% / auto-verify pass -> commit handoff
- session_replay_agreement 95%-99.9% / mark as degraded, produce regression diff report, require engineer signoff
- session_replay_agreement < 95% / automatic rollback and incident page creation
- handoff-duration-target < 2s (median) / if > 5s then fail fast to fallback pool

Instrumentation and required metrics (minimum):
- kernel.handoff.attempts (counter)
- kernel.handoff.success (counter)
- kernel.handoff.duration_ms (histogram)
- kernel.kv.snapshot_size_bytes (gauge)
- kernel.kv.missing_keys_during_replay (counter)
- kernel.replay.agreement_pct (gauge per session sampled)
- kernel.quant.meta_mismatch (counter)
- trace.session_id preserved (boolean per handoff)

Observability queries (examples):
- Reconciliation failure rate last 1h:
  - PromQL: sum(increase(kernel_replay_agreement_failures_total[1h])) / sum(increase(kernel.handoff.attempts[1h]))
- Sessions with missing KV keys:
  - PromQL: sum by (kernel_id) (increase(kernel_kv_missing_keys_during_replay_total[15m]))
- Latency impact of handoff:
  - LogQL: | json | handoff=false OR handoff=true | compare percentile(latency_ms,95, kernel)

Pre-check checklist (automated gating before any kernel rollout):
1) Canary cohort traffic mirror is configured (mirror ratio >= 0.02).
2) Snapshot size distribution within historical 95th percentile for target model.
3) Quantization profile compatibility matrix verified for target kernel version.
4) Observability sampling and tracing propagated for all canary requests.
5) Canary health probes (see health probe list) passing for 15 minutes.

Health probes (example list):
- probe /healthz/kernel -> returns OK + kernel_version + kv_snapshot_epoch
- probe /healthz/replay -> runs deterministic replay on a synthetic prefix corpus and returns agreement pct
- probe /metrics -> Prometheus scrape endpoint

Runbook: graceful kernel handoff (cooperative) - for SRE / oncall
1) Intent: move sessions from kernel A to kernel B for planned upgrade or maintenance.
2) Preconditions: B has been validated in staging, gating pre-checks passed, canary mirror warm.
3) Steps:
   a) Mark kernel A as "draining" in router config: set routing.weight(A)=0 over 30s window; router will forward new requests to other kernels while allowing in-flight to finish.
   b) Trigger snapshot: POST /internal/kernel/{A}/snapshot -> returns snapshot_id.
   c) Verify snapshot completeness: GET /internal/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/verify -> expect {"missing_keys":0, "meta_ok":true}. If missing_keys > 0 go to troubleshooting below.
   d) Transfer snapshot to B: POST /internal/kernel/{B}/ingest-snapshot {"snapshot_id": "..."}.
   e) Run local deterministic replay on B for sample prefixes: POST /internal/kernel/{B}/replay-sample -> returns agreement scores per prefix.
   f) If agreement >= 99.9% for sampled prefixes, mark commit: POST /internal/kernel/{B}/commit-handoff {"snapshot_id":"..."}. Router update: atomically swap session index pointers to B.
   g) Monitor for 15 minutes: replay.agreement_pct, kv.missing_keys, 95/99 latency. If any threshold violated, trigger rollback (see rollback flow).
4) Post-mortem: record snapshot_id, durations, sample diffs, and link to incident tracker.

Runbook: emergency handoff (preemptive eviction) - for critical capacity events
1) Intent: evict and migrate sessions from an overloaded node when cooperative drain not possible.
2) Preconditions: immediate capacity pressure, automated graceful drain failed or impossible.
3) Steps:
   a) Select victim kernel(s) using eviction scorer (eviction_score > configured_threshold).
   b) Create partial snapshot including most-recently-used KV ranges prioritized by active sessions. Limit snapshot duration to 500ms to bound tail latency.
   c) Ingest into fallback kernel pool (a pool running conservative kernels that accept smaller snapshots).
   d) Run targeted replay on highest-priority sessions only (top 1% traffic by token-volume).
   e) If replay agreement < 95% for any top-priority session: mark for immediate re-run with full snapshot and escalate to runtime-engineer.

Rollback flow (automated and manual)
- Automated rollback trigger: replay.agreement_pct < 95% OR kv.missing_keys_during_replay > 10 for any affected session cohort. System will:
  1) Re-point router session index back to source kernel snapshot_id (atomic pointer swap).
  2) Mark target kernel instance as failed and add to quarantine list.
  3) Create incident ticket and populate required fields (snapshot ids, sample diffs, metric deltas).
- Manual rollback requires engineer signoff and is used when automated rollback cannot be executed (e.g., persistent index corruption).

Troubleshooting matrix (common failure modes):
- Symptom: missing keys during replay
  - Likely causes: partial snapshot, metadata mismatch (namespace/versioning), or RPC truncation.
  - First actions: examine snapshot verification output, check transport logs for truncated payloads (s3/redis clamp errors), check kernel.kv.snapshot_size_bytes variance.

- Symptom: quantization metadata mismatch -> scaled logits differ
  - Likely causes: kernel compiled with different quantization layout, per-layer quantization rounding change, or precision-promote in kernel config.
  - First actions: compare kernel.build_metadata.quant_profile between A and B. If mismatch, abort commit and roll back.

- Symptom: replay agreement slightly degraded (99.0-99.8%)
  - Likely causes: non-determinism in floating ops at fringe layers, timing differences in fused kernels, or sampling variance in test corpus.
  - First actions: increase sample size for replay check, run deterministic microbench on fused kernel path, and if persistent, capture kernel traces for triage.

Reconciliation algorithm (recommended pseudocode):
```python
# high level pseudocode for deterministic reconciliation
def reconcile_snapshot(source_snapshot, target_kernel):
    # 1. validate metadata
    assert source_snapshot.model_id == target_kernel.model_id
    assert source_snapshot.quant_profile == target_kernel.quant_profile

    # 2. stream keys and apply in deterministic order (lexicographic by session_id, then seq_num)
    for session_id in sorted(source_snapshot.sessions):
        for ev in sorted(source_snapshot.sessions[session_id].events, key=lambda e: e.seq_num):
            target_kernel.apply_event(session_id, ev)

    # 3. run sampled deterministic forward passes and compare logits
    diffs = []
    for prefix in sample_prefixes():
        out_src = source_snapshot.simulate_forward(prefix)
        out_tgt = target_kernel.simulate_forward(prefix)
        diffs.append(cosine_similarity(out_src.logits, out_tgt.logits))

    return aggregate_agreement(diffs)
```
Upgrade and rollout policy (recommended):
1) Canary (1% mirrored traffic, 30m) -> 2) Extended canary (5% mirrored traffic, 2h) -> 3) Progressive roll (20% -> 50% -> 100%) with health gates at each step.
2) Automatic rollback gates for any step if replay.agreement drops below configured threshold for the cohort.
3) All rollouts must include a replay corpus and the snapshot archive stored with provenance tags.

Developer guidance for kernel authors (short):
- Maintain backward-compatible quant_profile changes; add feature flags and opt-in toggles for new fused kernels.
- Implement deterministic seeds for any non-deterministic code paths used during snapshot application and replay.
- Provide a unit-test harness: unit_replay_suite that can be executed with "./tools/unit_replay_suite --snapshot <id> --kernel <target>".

Post-incident checklist and artifacts required:
- snapshot_id(s), sample prefixes used, replay diffs, kernel build hashes for source and target, Prometheus metric snapshots (15m pre/post), traces (OTel) correlated to trace.session_id, and incident timeline.

Appendix A: Example CLI snippets
- Trigger snapshot (operator):
  curl -X POST http://runtime-internal/api/v1/kernel/alpha/snapshot -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"reason":"canary-rollout-2026-02"}'
- Verify snapshot:
  curl http://runtime-internal/api/v1/snapshots/<id>/verify | jq
- Ingest snapshot into target:
  curl -X POST http://runtime-internal/api/v1/kernel/beta/ingest-snapshot -d '{"snapshot_id":"<id>"}'

Appendix B: Minimum config example (YAML)
- gate:
    replay_sample_size: 50  # number of prefixes to check per snapshot
    min_agreement_pct: 99.9
    emergency_min_agreement_pct: 95.0
- snapshot:
    max_transfer_bytes: 1_200_000_000
    transfer_timeout_ms: 5000
- routing:
    graceful_drain_window_s: 30
    fallback_pool: "conservative-pool-v1"
